title: The determinant module of a finite length module over a local ring is at most one dimensional over the residue field
author: The Stacks Project Authors
work: Stacks Project, chapter chow.tex (Chow Homology and Chern Classes)
source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file chow.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
difficulty_reason: The statement is short but it is not self-contained: it says 'with notations as above' and asserts that dim_kappa(det_kappa(M)) <= 1 for a finite length module M over a local ring (R, m, kappa), where det_kappa is the determinant module built out of admissible sequences of M modulo the three admissible relations (statement lines 15760-15763). The proof cannot be a formal manipulation of the definition: it must pick an admissible sequence f_1,...,f_l with length_R(<f_1,...,f_i>) = i, then show that an arbitrary admissible sequence e_1,...,e_l either has vanishing symbol [e_1,...,e_l] = 0 (when it does not generate M) or can be transformed into a scalar multiple of the chosen symbol by repeatedly locating the smallest index with f_1 in <e_1,...,e_i>, writing e_i = lambda f_1 + x with lambda a unit, and applying the second and third admissible relations i-1 times to move f_1 to the front, followed by an induction on j (proof lines 15766-15818). The order of the admissible sequences, the unit, and the sign (-1)^{i-1} are exactly the content of the argument, so the claim is H2.
